questions.question: After students get off the bus at school, the driver should:

options.text: Assume students took all their belongings.
Assume students cleared the doorway right away.
Walk through the bus to check for any sleeping or hiding students.
Turn off the dispatch radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for any sleeping or hiding students.
questions.explanation: After students leave, the driver must walk through the bus to look for any students still on board who may be sleeping or hiding. The driver should also check for items students left behind.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following except:

options.text: Wear your safety belt.
Obey all traffic signs.
Finish the test without an accident.
Show that you can use your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that you can use your cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: During the on-road test, you must drive safely. This means wearing your safety belt, obeying all traffic signs and laws, and finishing without accidents or violations. You should never use a cell phone while driving.

questions.question: When stopping to pick up students, a bus driver should:

options.text: Put the vehicle in park.
Put the vehicle in first gear.
Put the vehicle in reverse.
Put the vehicle in third gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in park.
questions.explanation: Always put the bus in park when stopping to pick up students. If the bus does not have a park gear, use neutral instead.

questions.question: When should you check the mirrors on a bus?

options.text: Before you start driving
While you are driving
After you finish driving
You do not need to check the mirrors

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving
questions.explanation: Always check the mirrors before you start driving. Adjust them as needed before you begin your trip.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Do an alley dock.
Parallel park to your right.
Parallel park to your left.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset parking in both directions, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a cargo lift, you should check that:

options.text: The lift is loosely attached.
The lift is not leaking.
The lift is fully extended.
The lift is the right color.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lift is not leaking.
questions.explanation: Check the cargo lift for leaks, damage, or missing parts. The lift must be fully closed and locked in place before driving.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following except:

options.text: Wear your safety belt.
Obey all traffic laws.
Finish the test without a traffic violation.
Obey traffic signs and signals only when other vehicles are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey traffic signs and signals only when other vehicles are present.
questions.explanation: You must always drive safely and responsibly. This means wearing your safety belt and obeying all traffic signs, signals, and laws at all times—even when no other traffic is present.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, drivers can:

options.text: Not exit the vehicle to check its position.
Leave the vehicle but are advised not to.
Exit only if the vehicle is in reverse.
Exit only if the vehicle is in neutral with the parking brake set.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit only if the vehicle is in neutral with the parking brake set.
questions.explanation: You can exit the vehicle during the test to check its position, but only after putting it in neutral and setting the parking brake. You may check the position no more than twice, except for straight line backing, where you may check only once.

questions.question: If a school bus needs to be evacuated, passengers should:

options.text: Always use the back door.
Always use the windows.
Always use the front door.
Use whichever exit is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever exit is safest.
questions.explanation: In an emergency evacuation, the driver must quickly decide which exit or exits are safest and direct passengers to use them.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, you must show all of the following except:

options.text: The oil pressure gauge is working.
The oil pressure warning light turns off, or the gauge shows normal pressure.
The oil temperature gauge rises to the normal operating range.
The oil pressure gauge comes on when the brakes are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: The oil pressure gauge comes on when the brakes are used.
questions.explanation: Check that the oil pressure gauge works. The warning light should turn off, or the gauge should show normal or increasing pressure. If the vehicle has an oil temperature gauge, it should gradually rise to normal operating temperature. The oil pressure gauge should not come on when brakes are used.

questions.question: How far before a school bus stop should the flashing lights turn on?

options.text: At least 50 feet
At least 100 feet
At least 200 feet
At least 1,000 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 200 feet
questions.explanation: School buses with flashing amber lights must turn them on at least 200 feet before stopping, unless state law says otherwise.

questions.question: What happens if you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: You fail only that exercise.
You must redo that exercise.
You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
You lose one point.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For buses, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly means you automatically fail the entire test.

questions.question: Why should a school bus stop a short distance from waiting students?

options.text: Students must walk to the bus, so the driver can watch them better.
Students are usually waiting on a sidewalk.
Students may be scared if the bus comes too close.
School buses are hard to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students must walk to the bus, so the driver can watch them better.
questions.explanation: A school bus should stop at least 10 feet away from waiting students. This makes students walk toward the bus, so the driver can watch them carefully.

questions.question: During the on-road test, you are evaluated on checking traffic. Which should you NOT do?

options.text: Scan the road for pedestrians.
Check traffic regularly.
Skip checking your mirrors near intersections.
Check your mirrors regularly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip checking your mirrors near intersections.
questions.explanation: Always check for traffic and use your mirrors regularly, especially at intersections. Scan for pedestrians wherever they might be.

questions.question: What counts as a look during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Walking to the back of the vehicle to check its position
Using side mirrors to check the vehicle's position
Looking out the driver's side window to check the vehicle's position
Glancing over your shoulder to check blind spots

questions.correctAnswerText: Walking to the back of the vehicle to check its position
questions.explanation: A look means opening your door, leaving your seat, and walking to the back of the vehicle to check its position. During straight line backing, you may look only once. During other exercises, you may look only twice.

questions.question: Who should establish a school bus stop?

options.text: The driver can add stops as needed.
The students should vote on stops.
Stops may change based on weather.
The school district authorities should establish stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: The school district authorities should establish stops.
questions.explanation: Drivers cannot change bus stop locations without written permission from school district officials.

questions.question: Backing a school bus is:

options.text: Strongly encouraged.
Strongly discouraged.
Only done in the morning.
Only done with students guiding you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strongly discouraged.
questions.explanation: Backing a school bus should be avoided. Only back up if there is no other way to move the vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on an expressway during the skills test?

options.text: Change lanes frequently.
Use your mirrors to check traffic as needed.
Drive on the left side of the lane.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors to check traffic as needed.
questions.explanation: On the expressway during the test, keep proper lane position, vehicle spacing, and speed. Continuously check traffic in all directions using your mirrors.

questions.question: During the pre-trip inspection test, what will you do?

options.text: Explain what you know about the pre-trip inspection process.
Watch someone else inspect your vehicle.
Watch a film about vehicle inspection.
Change all the tires on your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you know about the pre-trip inspection process.
questions.explanation: During the inspection test, you must do a complete vehicle inspection. You must explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: How should students board a school bus?

options.text: In a single-file line.
Two at a time.
In large groups.
However they want. It makes no difference.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Students should board slowly in a single-file line while holding the handrails.
